en: A first-class lever like a seesaw multiplies force when the fulcrum is placed closer to the heavy load.
An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the lifting force needed by increasing the distance the object moves.
Rough sandpaper increases sliding friction against wood, converting kinetic energy into heat and slowing the movement.
Earth's gravity pulls objects toward its center, causing a dropped ball to continuously accelerate as it falls.
An electromagnet generates a magnetic field only when electric current flows through its coiled copper wire.
Rubbing a balloon on hair transfers electrons, creating a negative charge that attracts positively charged wall surfaces.
Light bends when passing from air into water because it slows down in the denser liquid medium.
Plucking a tight guitar string creates vibrations that push air molecules, transmitting sound waves to your ears.
Heat conducts through a metal spoon in hot soup as fast-moving particles collide with slower neighboring particles.
A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy that transforms into kinetic energy when released to snap forward.
Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of moving air into electrical energy by spinning internal generator magnets.
A fixed pulley changes the direction of your applied force, allowing you to pull down to lift objects.
